message.content:
Below is a concise “long‑weekend” calendar for Canada in 2023.  
A long weekend is defined as a statutory holiday that falls on a **Friday** or a **Monday** (or is observed on a Monday when the actual holiday falls on a weekend).  These dates automatically give you a three‑day break without needing to request extra leave.

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Province(s) where it’s a statutory holiday | Long‑weekend status |
|-------------|---------|-------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| **Jan 2** (Mon) | New Year’s Day (observed) | All provinces & territories | ✔️ (Dec 31–Jan 2) |
| **Feb 20** (Mon) | Family Day | Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Manitoba | ✔️ |
| **Apr 7** (Fri) | Good Friday | Most provinces (except Quebec) | ✔️ |
| **May 22** (Mon) | Victoria Day | All provinces & territories | ✔️ |
| **Jul 3** (Mon) | Canada Day (observed) | All provinces & territories | ✔️ (Jul 1–3) |
| **Sep 4** (Mon) | Labour Day | All provinces & territories | ✔️ |
| **Oct 9** (Mon) | Thanksgiving | All provinces & territories | ✔️ |
| **Dec 25** (Mon) | Christmas | All provinces & territories | ✔️ |

### Quick notes

* **New Year’s Day (observed)** – Since Jan 1, 2023 was a Sunday, the holiday is observed on Monday, Jan 2.  
* **Canada Day (observed)** – July 1, 2023 fell on a Saturday, so the holiday is observed on Monday, Jul 3.  
* **Family Day** – Only applies in the provinces listed; other provinces have different spring holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador on Mar 17, 2023 – a Thursday, which can be turned into a long weekend if you take Friday off).  
* **Good Friday** – A statutory holiday in most provinces (not Quebec).  

Feel free to plug these dates directly into your holiday‑planning app. If you need province‑specific long weekends beyond the ones listed above, let me know!
